proposal.title: IBM conversational assistant – first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: an authenticated chat for synthetic users with per-user state, bounded context, watsonx.ai runtime and human escalation. No external actions. Assumptions: region not selected; watsonx.ai model, plan and account access are unverified. No native Terraform generator exists for this IBM path yet, so engineering is still required. The context limiter is application logic inside Code Engine.

data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: Synthetic test user signing in through a browser. This is a client reference and is not provisioned.

data.label: Sign-in
data.description: Issues OIDC tokens to synthetic users. The app validates the tokens and derives the user ID from the token subject.

data.label: Chat application
data.description: Web UI and chat API. Rejects unauthenticated requests, loads and saves per-user history, builds the bounded prompt, calls the model and returns the reply. It has no tools for external actions.

data.label: Conversation state
data.description: Stores per-user conversation documents, partitioned by the token subject. The app can only read and write the signed-in user's own partition. Retention is still to be decided.

data.label: Bounded context builder
data.description: Application logic owned by the Chat application, not a separate deployment. It limits history turns, input size and output tokens, and treats stored content as untrusted.

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Foundation model inference via the watsonx.ai API using a service ID. The model, plan, region and access are unverified. Local tests use a scripted mock instead.

data.label: Escalation
data.description: The app publishes an escalation event when the user asks for a person or the model abstains. The event goes to the reviewer's destination.

data.label: Human reviewer
data.description: The person who receives escalated conversations. Not provisioned.

data.label: Logs & audit
data.description: Application logs, escalation audit and account activity. Retention is still to be decided.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents one user's conversations from leaking to another user.
requirementDrafts.statement: Only authenticated users can chat. Each user can read and continue only their own conversation history, and unknown or invalid tokens are rejected.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Controls cost, latency and prompt-injection exposure. The limit values are still to be confirmed.
requirementDrafts.basis: "bounded context" and "No external actions in this first test"
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: each model call has limits on history turns, input size and output tokens. No external actions are performed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Gives users a safe fallback when the assistant cannot help. The exact triggers need confirmation.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: an explicit request for a person, or a model abstention, creates an escalation that is notified to a human reviewer and audited.

An empty failures list NEVER means a sound, complete or correct design. Celebrate only named checks that actually passed. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. response.message: No runtime tests have run yet, so nothing is validated. The empty failures list only means emulation stopped before any check could start. The first blocker is that none of our IBM components (App ID, Code Engine, Cloudant, watsonx.ai, Event Notifications) has a supported generated implementation. Today the only IBM contract is private object storage, and moving to it would cut our assistant down to storage, which we've agreed not to do. That makes this a product engineering task, not a design mistake. The reproducer is revision 2, artifact 03f1ce7d…, which shows 8 "Implementation needed" gaps. So the diagram stays as it is. One more point: the synthetic user and the human reviewer don't need to be built, only referenced, but we do need to write down how each one is identified. While that engineering work happens, we can keep firming up the design: how long should synthetic conversation history be kept before it's deleted (for example 7 days, 30 days, or not sure)?
